source_control.primary: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 (June 2012)
source_control.current_law_support: National Road Traffic Act 93 of 1996 for sections 63-64
source_control.note: Items with legal_review_status=pending remain held from release certification until current regulations are checked.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.3 — Dipped beam

en.title: Dipped beam
en.key_point: A dipped-beam headlamp must be adjusted and maintained so that it adequately lights the road ahead.
en.explanation: The official learner manual says dipped beam must allow the driver or rider to see a person, vehicle or substantial object at least 45 metres ahead. This distance remains held for current-regulation verification before release certification.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.4 — Parking lamps

en.title: Parking lamps
en.key_point: Do not drive a moving vehicle on a public road using only its parking lamps.
en.explanation: Parking lamps are not a substitute for the normal lamps required while the vehicle is being driven.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.5 — Rear lamps

en.title: Rear lamps
en.key_point: A motorcycle and a light motor vehicle used on a public road must have rear lighting that shows red to the rear.
en.explanation: Rear lamps make the vehicle visible from behind. The exact current equipment wording is being cross-checked against the operative regulations before final release certification.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.6 — Stop lamp

en.title: Stop lamps
en.key_point: A light motor vehicle or motorcycle used on a public road must have rear stop lamps that show red when braking.
en.explanation: A stop lamp warns following road users that the vehicle is slowing or stopping. Detailed visibility measurements remain under current-regulation verification.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.7 — Number plate lamp

en.title: Number-plate lamp
en.key_point: A motor vehicle used on a public road must have a rear number-plate lamp that illuminates the registration plate.
en.explanation: The purpose is to keep the registration plate visible at night. The manual's exact distance requirement remains under current-regulation verification.

source.locator: National Road Traffic Act 93 of 1996 §63 — Reckless or negligent driving

en.title: Reckless or negligent driving
en.key_point: A person may not drive a vehicle on a public road recklessly or negligently.
en.explanation: Road conditions, traffic, speed and the manner of driving all matter when deciding whether driving was reckless or negligent.

source.locator: National Road Traffic Act 93 of 1996 §64 — Inconsiderate driving

en.title: Inconsiderate driving
en.key_point: A person may not drive on a public road without reasonable consideration for other people using the road.
en.explanation: Safe driving includes consideration for other road users, not only avoiding a collision or breaking a speed limit.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.37 — Driving on divided public road

en.title: Driving on a divided public road
en.key_point: Use the left-hand roadway unless a traffic sign or traffic officer directs or permits you to use another roadway.
en.explanation: Where a public road is divided into separate roadways, traffic normally keeps to the left-hand roadway.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.38 — Driving on left side of roadway

en.title: Keep left on the roadway
en.key_point: Drive on the left side of the roadway and do not unnecessarily encroach into the right half.
en.explanation: Move left safely when another vehicle wants to pass and do not accelerate until it has passed.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.39 — Prohibition on driving on shoulder except in certain circumstances

en.title: Driving on the shoulder
en.key_point: Do not normally drive on the shoulder. A light vehicle may use it only in limited safe circumstances allowed by the rules.
en.explanation: The learner manual describes daytime use while being overtaken, provided it is safe and visibility is adequate. The exact conditions remain under the current-regulation verification gate.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.40 — Lane changing

en.title: Changing lanes
en.key_point: Change from one marked lane to another only when you can do so without obstructing or endangering other traffic.
en.explanation: Check mirrors and blind spots, signal in good time and move only when there is a safe gap.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.42 — Direction indicators

en.title: Direction indicators
en.key_point: Use direction indicators when turning or changing lanes.
en.explanation: Indicators communicate your intended movement to other road users. Vehicle-equipment details remain subject to the current-regulation check.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.43.1 — Motorcycle retro-reflector

en.title: Motorcycle rear reflector
en.key_point: A motorcycle used on a public road must have a red retro-reflector fitted at the rear.
en.explanation: The reflector helps other road users see the motorcycle from behind in low-light conditions.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.43.2 — Light motor vehicle retro-reflectors

en.title: Light-vehicle rear reflectors
en.key_point: A light motor vehicle must have red retro-reflectors at the rear.
en.explanation: The learner manual specifies one on each side. The exact current equipment wording is being checked against operative regulations.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.45 — Overtaking/passing, limited left-passing exceptions

en.title: Passing on the left
en.key_point: Overtaking is normally on the right. Passing on the left is allowed only in specific safe situations permitted by the rules.
en.explanation: Do not treat the left side as a general overtaking lane. The detailed exceptions remain tied to the official rule set and current-regulation check.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.50 — Duties relating to motorcycles

en.title: Motorcycle rider control
en.key_point: Ride so that you maintain complete control of the motorcycle and a clear view of the road and traffic.
en.explanation: Baggage must be carried so that it does not obstruct your view or prevent proper control.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.50 — Rider/passenger must not take hold of another moving vehicle

en.title: Do not hold onto another moving vehicle
en.key_point: A motorcycle rider or passenger must not take hold of another vehicle that is moving.
en.explanation: The motorcycle must be controlled independently and safely at all times.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.50 — Motorcycles in single file, subject to overtaking rule

en.title: Motorcycles travelling together
en.key_point: Motorcycles travelling in the same lane should ride in single file, except as allowed while overtaking.
en.explanation: The rule reduces conflict between motorcycles sharing the same lane and other road users.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.51 — Sidecar attachment

en.title: Motorcycle sidecar
en.key_point: A sidecar used on a public road must be attached on the correct side of the motorcycle.
en.explanation: The learner manual specifies the left side and contains an engine-capacity condition. Those equipment details remain under current-regulation verification.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.54 — Vehicle left/abandoned

en.title: Leaving a vehicle on a public road
en.key_point: Do not leave a vehicle standing indefinitely on a public road.
en.explanation: The learner manual sets different time periods inside and outside urban areas. Those exact periods remain under the current-regulation verification gate before release certification.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.55 — Damage to public roads

en.title: Do not damage the road
en.key_point: Do not operate or move a vehicle in a way that damages the roadway.
en.explanation: The manual also prohibits deliberately dragging or spinning wheels on the road except in an emergency.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.56 — Freeways: prohibited vehicles/users

en.title: Who may use a freeway
en.key_point: Not every road user or vehicle is allowed on a freeway.
en.explanation: The official learner manual excludes several slow or unsuitable road users and vehicle types. Exact category thresholds remain under current-regulation verification.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.56 — Freeway stopping, pedestrians/animals and merging

en.title: Freeway behaviour
en.key_point: Do not stop on a freeway except where the rules allow it, and remain alert to vehicles merging from on-ramps.
en.explanation: The manual also restricts pedestrians and animals on freeways and requires drivers to allow a vehicle ahead to merge safely from an on-ramp.
